Our clients are business owners, and they want to see us in person. Email doesn't build those relationships. If you'd rather manage accounts from your inbox, this isn't the job.

**What's hard about it**

There's no script. You'll manage a lot of client relationships at once, so you need to stay organized and follow through. You'll also travel regularly to clients within a couple hours' drive of Atlanta.

**Who you are**

Maybe you've managed accounts for a payroll company, an insurance agency, a bank or a distributor. You don't need a tax or accounting background. You do need to be someone who:

* Does what they say they'll do
* Is comfortable sitting down with a business owner or CFO
* Spots opportunities and brings them back to the team
* Stays organized across a lot of clients

Skilled Wound Care is hiring an Entry Level Medical Sales Representative (Business Development Associate) for a nationwide, field-based travel role. **Position Title:** Community Outreach Specialist – Family Connects Chicago (FCC) Community Alignment – West Region

**Department:** Foster Care

**About the Program:**

The Family Connects Chicago (FCC) Community Alignment System strengthens the ecosystem of supports for birthing people and newborns by improving hyperlocal outreach, referral coordination, and community voice in neighborhoods experiencing the greatest disparities in infant mortality and maternal health outcomes. UCAN will serve as the Community Alignment Delegate for the West Region, embedding FCC within trusted West Side networks. The program advances CDPH’s four objectives: (1) outreach in priority areas; (2) systems improvement to strengthen referral pathways; (3) community engagement to elevate parent voice; and (4) coordination to ensure a unified citywide system. UCAN’s established trauma-informed infrastructure in North Lawndale and Garfield Park allows immediate implementation. The program formalizes navigation and alignment activities that UCAN already performs, ensuring that families identified through FCC nurse home visits are successfully connected to behavioral health, housing supports, food access, safe sleep resources, and other essential services.

  

**Position Objective and Summary:**

The Community Outreach Specialist is a frontline, community-based role responsible for engaging West Side residents, raising awareness of Family Connects Chicago (FCC), and connecting pregnant and postpartum caregivers to navigation, resources, and infant essentials through hyperlocal outreach and events.

* Conduct door-to-door canvassing, tabling, and other outreach activities in priority West Region neighborhoods.
* Attend and help organize community events (e.g., baby showers, resource fairs, health events) to promote FCC and share key public health messages.

* Participate in regular team meetings, trainings, and reflective supervision sessions.

* Strong interpersonal and communication skills; ability to engage comfortably with community members in diverse settings.
* Bilingual (English/Spanish) strongly preferred for at least one position.
* Ability to work flexible hours, including some evenings and weekends.

**Exhibit Operations Specialist I**

**Full-Time Temporary**

**Non-Exempt**

**Union Position**

**About the Adler Planetarium**

The Adler Planetarium connects people to the universe and each other. Whether introducing a guest to the Ring Nebula, a neighborhood school to a community partner, a research team to a network of citizen scientists, or one staff member to another, the Adler's focus on meaningful connections dates back nearly a century.

Today, the museum typically hosts close to 400,000 visitors annually and reaches millions more through youth STEAM programs, neighborhood skywatching events, online citizen science, and other outreach efforts. With the Adlers' support, people of all ages, backgrounds, and abilities gain the confidence to learn more about science and space discovery, and to explore their universe together under the sky we all share.

**The Position**

The Adler Planetarium is seeking a Full-Time Temporary Exhibit Operations Specialist I to join our dynamic team on Chicago's Museum Campus. This position opens and closes exhibits, performs routine cleaning and maintenance, and ensures all guest-facing areas are always ready for guests. Daily duties include conducting routine rounds, cleaning and maintaining exhibits and galleries, managing trash disposal, and maintaining exhibits, galleries, displays, and design lab spaces. Additional responsibilities may include assisting with exhibit team projects such as new exhibit installations, patching, painting, graphic installation, and maintaining exhibit components as needed. This is a union position with the Adler Planetarium Workers United, AFSCME Council 31.

This individual will also be responsible for:

* Opening and closing museum exhibits and galleries, including powering on/off interactive components, equipment, computers, and lighting
* Ensuring all areas are clean, guest-ready, and maintained in safe, proper working order
* Supporting Exhibits staff during sponsored evening events as assigned
* Conducting daily inspections of exhibits, galleries, displays, community design lab spaces, and signage to assess cleanliness, condition, and wear
* Identifying cleaning or maintenance needs and performing minor upkeep tasks as needed
* Responding to radio calls by addressing issues directly when possible or escalating to Exhibit Technicians or other staff as appropriate
* Performing routine cleaning tasks, including scrubbing surfaces, removing dirt and debris, and vacuuming
* Monitoring exhibit components for wear and tear, performing preventive maintenance and minor repairs, such as replacing lights, batteries, switches, keyboards, and physical interactive elements
* Emptying trash receptacles and transferring waste to dumpsters
* Vacuuming exhibit and workspace areas and assisting with material handling, including loading and unloading trucks related to exhibits and exhibit workspaces
* Assisting with larger scheduled maintenance and team projects on a monthly, biannual, or annual basis, including cleaning and dusting exhibit components, repainting galleries, replacing or installing graphics and signage, and supporting new exhibit production efforts
* Presenting a positive, customer-facing experience by maintaining a neat and professional appearance, treating guests with respect, and assisting visitors in making their experience exceptional when engaged

The typical work schedule for this position is 35 hours per week, Sunday through Thursday, 7 am-3 pm or 8:30 am-4:30 pm, and Wednesday.

* 7- to 35-hour workweek
* Eligible to accrue up to 6 vacation days per year
* 3 sick days as of the date of hire (can accrue up to 6.5 days per year)
* Eligible to earn time and a half for working on any of the 7 Adler observed holidays
* Flexible work arrangements
* Paid Family Bereavement Leave & Jury Duty
* Paid Parental Leave

Commuter flexible spending account

Retirement Savings Plan

* Adler match is 100% vested immediately
* Eligible to enroll as of the date of hire

Network of Support through our EAP programs

* Resources to help address emotional, legal, and financial issues
* Face-to-face, telephonic, and web-based services
* Free subscription to the Calm Premium app

Employee Loan Program

Discounted Onsite Parking Program

Free Entrance to Chicago area museums and cultural institutions

**The Person**

The ideal candidate is a reliable, detail-oriented team member with hands-on technical skills and a strong commitment to guest safety and experience. This role requires practical fabrication and maintenance experience, the ability to work independently and collaboratively, and sound judgment when responding to operational or safety concerns in a public-facing museum environment.
